name: swatch
description: A swatch shows a small sample of a fill — such as a color, gradient, texture, or material — that is intended to be applied to an object.

documentBlocks.content: A swatch shows a small sample of a fill — such as a color, gradient, texture, or material — that is intended to be applied to an object.

Keyboard focus.

A swatch can be navigated using a keyboard. The keyboard focus state adds a blue ring to the swatch in focus.

Mixed value.

When a swatch represents multiple values that are not identical, the preview shows a gray fill and a dash UI icon.

Hide unavailable swatches when possible.

Even though swatches can have a disabled state, hiding unavailable swatches reduces visual clutter and eases cognitive load. Only show disabled swatches if hiding them would cause confusion to your users.

Keyboard interactions.

Key Interaction Tab Moves focus onto or off of the swatch group. Focus moves to the first swatch in the group. Space or Enter Triggers an action or selects the swatch when selection is enabled. The focus remains on the swatch, unless the swatch opens or closes the current container. In this case, the focus moves to the target or back to the caller.

Cursor guidelines.

Cursor Description Pointer Use the pointer cursor for all interactive elements in every state.

WCAG 2.2 compliance.

Any criterion not mention in the below table are not applicable to this component or are resolved with underlying requirements, engineering, and styles of the entire system. 1. Perceivable Requirement Criterion Level Compliance Non-text content 1.1.1 A Non‑text elements must provide a text alternative that communicates the control’s purpose. All controls, especially icon‑only controls, need an accessible name (for example, via a title, aria‑label, or associated text) so screen readers can announce their function. Info and relationships, Identify purpose 1.3.1, 1.3.6 A, AAA Swatch groups should be understandable by assistive technologies like screen readers. This means the proper semantic HTML or ARIA role should be utilized, so the grouping relationship between swatches and the selected state are programmatically conveyed. Use of color 1.4.1 A This criterion requires that color not be the only method of communicating information. In swatches, the color itself is the content being presented, not a cue that conveys additional meaning. 2. Operable Requirement Criterion Level Compliance Keyboard 2.1.1, 2.1.3 A, AAA All functionality of the component is operable through a keyboard without specific timing for keystrokes. Keyboard traps 2.1.2 A Focus can be moved away from the component using only a keyboard. Seizures and physical reactions 2.3.1, 2.3.2, 2.3.3 A, AAA, AAA There is no flashing content or unnecessary motion or animation in this component. Focus order 2.4.3 A Navigation sequences receive focus in an order that preserves meaning and operability. Focus visible 2.4.7 AA Keyboard states use an indicator that is visible with at least 3:1 contrast.

preview.description: The swatch color, as a CSS color: #rgb, #rrggbb (with an optional alpha) or rgb() and rgba(), or a linear-gradient() of those colors. Unset or fully transparent draws the empty slash. Images are not drawn.

value.description: What the swatch stands for (Figma Value). default shows the preview color (None is an unset preview); mixed shows a gray fill and a dash when it represents several different values; add shows the add button background and glyph.

cornerRounding.description: Determines the corner radius of the swatch. Partial refers to corner-radius-75.

anatomy.name: container
anatomy.description: Frame of the swatch: its size, shape and corner rounding. The hairline border, the selected 2px border and the inner band are container styling (owner decision C1).

anatomy.name: opacity-checkerboard
anatomy.description: Pattern behind a preview color with alpha below 1; sized m. It sits before fill, so the color draws over it.

anatomy.name: fill
anatomy.description: The preview color. The slash and icon sit on it.

anatomy.name: slash
anatomy.description: Diagonal slash indicating an empty or "none" swatch.

anatomy.name: icon
anatomy.description: Cancel glyph drawn over a disabled swatch.

anatomy.name: focus-indicator
anatomy.description: Ring drawn around the swatch for keyboard focus.

anatomy.name: tooltip
anatomy.description: Floating label shown when the swatch is hovered; a nested component placed outside the swatch, like picker menu-container. The gap from the container to it is a space-between record.

anatomyReview.notes: Proposed from Figma S2 Web (Swatch: background, opacity checkerboard instance, border, inner border when selected, slash for the None value, Cancel icon when disabled) and React Spectrum ColorSwatch and ColorSwatchPicker (fill, checkerboard, slash, selection border and inner band, focusRing). SWC gen2 has no swatch. Hover draws a Tooltip in Figma (its own component) and down changes nothing, so both are notVisual. The disabled Cancel look is Figma only. Reviewed by the owner 2026-11-18. A7 (2026-11-20), owner decisions C1 and C2: border and inner-border are not parts. The hairline is a container stroke; the selected 2px border and the inner band are border records pinned isSelected, and the band colour is the border color pinned position inner (the recipe's innerStroke selects it with position inner). opacity-checkerboard is a nested component (size m) before fill; the recipe nests it. Owner decision C12: Figma Value Mixed and Add are the option `value` (default, mixed, add): the dash and add glyphs are on icon, the Add background on container. Figma only; React Spectrum and SWC have no such swatch. Owner decision C13: tooltip is a top-level part (Figma draws a Tooltip on hover; React Spectrum has none). It is a nested component, but the anatomy `component` field is not built, so it is declared as a plain part like picker menu-container.
